title: Which of these four pairs of numbers are safe?
description: The factors of the numbers in each pair are listed and compared, and the pairs with no shared factor besides one are marked safe. Keeko doubts that four and fifteen can be safe, because neither is prime.
teaching_notes: One idea: a pair is safe when its two factor lists share only one. Watch for students who think a safe pair needs a prime number in it.

source: Check if these pairs are safe: a. 15 and 39, b. 4 and 15, c.
video_script.why: The child lists the factors of both numbers in each pair and looks for a shared factor other than one.
video_script.substitution: List the factors of both numbers in a pair and mark the pair safe only when just one is shared.
video_script.anchor: Four pairs of number cards, each with a factor list under it
video_script.wrong_answer: four and fifteen cannot be safe
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks four and fifteen cannot be safe because neither is prime, but their factor lists share only one, so the pair is safe.
video_script.payoff_line: Four and fifteen are safe, and eighteen and twenty nine are safe.

final_answer.spoken: two of the four pairs are safe

maths_rules: a pair is safe when it has no common factor other than 1
video_script.design: Four pairs of cards each get two factor lists; a shared factor other than one glows amber and a pair with only one shared turns teal.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; four pairs of number cards: 15 and 39, 4 and 15, 18 and 29, 20 and 55

marks.first: the first two pairs of cards appear
marks.second: the last two pairs of cards appear and a question mark rises over all four

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about safe pairs.
<bookmark mark='first'/>Four pairs are given. The first two are fifteen and thirty nine, and four and fifteen.
<bookmark mark='second'/>The last two are eighteen and twenty nine, and twenty and fifty five. Which pairs are safe?

beats.on_screen: the four pairs stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: safe pair = no jump size except 1 reaches both = no common factor other than 1

marks.safe: the word safe appears beside a pair that no jump size reaches
marks.common: the words common factor appear and join the two factor lists

narration: <bookmark mark='safe'/>A pair is safe when no jump size except one reaches both numbers.
<bookmark mark='common'/>That means the two numbers have no common factor other than one.

marks.given: the four pairs are written in a row

beats.on_screen: To find: which pairs have no common factor other than 1

marks.find: the words to find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find which pairs are safe.

marks.fifteen: the lists for fifteen and thirty nine are drawn and the shared three glows in amber
marks.twenty: the lists for twenty and fifty five are drawn and the shared five glows in amber

narration: <bookmark mark='fifteen'/>Step one, list the factors. Fifteen and thirty nine share the factor three, so that pair is not safe.
<bookmark mark='twenty'/>Twenty and fifty five share the factor five, so that pair is not safe either.

marks.four: the lists for four and fifteen are drawn and only one is joined
marks.eighteen: the lists for eighteen and twenty nine are drawn and only one is joined

narration: <bookmark mark='four'/>Step two, check the other pairs. Four has one, two and four, and fifteen has one, three, five and fifteen. Only one is shared.
<bookmark mark='eighteen'/>Twenty nine has only the factors one and twenty nine, and eighteen does not have twenty nine. Only one is shared.

beats.on_screen: Check: 2 pairs share a factor, 2 pairs share only 1; 4 pairs in all

marks.safe: the other two pairs are marked teal

narration: <bookmark mark='two'/>Step three, count the pairs. Two pairs share a factor besides one.
<bookmark mark='safe'/>The other two share only one, which makes four pairs in all.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Four and fifteen are safe, and eighteen and twenty nine are safe.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the answer
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's doubt: 4 and 15 cannot be safe because neither is prime, crossed out; 4: 1, 2, 4 and 15: 1, 3, 5, 15 share only 1

marks.doubt: Keeko's doubt appears in a bubble
marks.reason: the two factor lists are written beside the bubble

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks four and fifteen cannot be safe, because neither of them is prime.
<bookmark mark='reason'/>But the lists of factors share only one.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Safe depends on shared factors, so the numbers need not be prime.
